content_voiceover: This is a quick self test on stem cell transplant indications under current TPOG-ALL therapy. The question asks which of four clinical scenarios should prompt a recommendation for hematopoietic stem cell transplant. Scenario one is a high risk B-ALL patient whose MRD had turned negative but then became positive again, meaning MRD recurrence. Scenario two is a high risk B-ALL patient who completed two courses of blinatumomab but still has positive MRD. Scenario three is a T-ALL patient who completed early intensification plus venetoclax therapy but still has positive MRD. Scenario four is a KMT2A rearranged infant ALL patient who completed venetoclax containing and blinatumomab therapy with positive MRD, then received second line therapy and became MRD negative. Working through the logic from the prior slides: scenario one clearly qualifies, since MRD recurrence after negativity is a standard transplant indication. Scenario two qualifies too, since persistent MRD positivity despite maximal blinatumomab therapy in high risk B-ALL is a treatment failure warranting transplant. Scenario three also qualifies, mirroring the ETP pathway where persistent MRD after venetoclax based intensification triggers transplant. Scenario four is the interesting one: even though the patient achieved MRD negativity after second line therapy, the infant protocol schema specifically shows that after second line therapy, an MRD negative result still routes to HSCT rather than continuing chemotherapy alone, because that MRD positivity after first line venetoclax and blinatumomab already signaled high risk disease. So the correct answer combines all four scenarios, which is answer E, one plus two plus three plus four.
keypoints: Scenario one, MRD recurrence after prior negativity, is a classic HSCT indication
Scenario two, persistent MRD positive despite two blinatumomab courses in high-risk B-ALL, warrants HSCT
Scenario three, persistent MRD positive after venetoclax-based intensification in T-ALL, warrants HSCT
Scenario four, infant ALL becoming MRD negative only after second-line therapy, still warrants HSCT
The correct answer is E, all four scenarios call for hematopoietic stem cell transplant
keypoint_voiceover: To recap this test question. All four scenarios turn out to warrant transplant: MRD recurrence after negativity, persistent MRD despite full blinatumomab therapy in high-risk B-ALL, persistent MRD after venetoclax intensification in T-ALL, and even an infant ALL patient who only achieves MRD negativity after switching to second-line therapy, since that late response still reflects high risk disease. So the correct answer is E, all four combined.
